summary: Mostly it sounds like DUMMIES. FARSIGHT copy is dry and procedural, and the barks are worker voice with real personality. The problems are a few barks and toasts that state things the sim did not log, one cue-key entry with no glyph, and two cue meanings that overpromise or hard-code a value.

issues.rule: Barks must match the logged event, and a catch-all impact bark must not deny a hit the sim recorded. The prototype line is only valid when it fits.
issues.fix: Impact recorded. I have a delivery to make.

issues.rule: Barks never assert facts the simulation did not establish. The admit event logs only car, class, model and lane, not any deadline pressure.
The toast fires when the drone flies in. It must not claim the cone is already moved, since the sim has not logged that yet.
issues.fix: FARSIGHT drone dispatched. Cone is blocking a car.

issues.found: {"cue":"blind","label":"Cannot see you","meaning":"The car has no sight of the dummy and keeps its speed."}
issues.rule: The cue key lists the grammar the field actually draws, each line beside its real glyph. P1 has no glyph for an unsighted car. The hidden-dummy behaviour in LOG#P1.7 has no cue.

issues.found: The car has fixed its plan and will follow it.
issues.rule: A committed manoeuvre is never re-planned, but safety braking can interrupt it. 'Will follow it' overpromises and contradicts the interrupted cue.
issues.fix: The car has fixed its plan. Only safety braking interrupts it.

issues.found: The car has been blocked for more than 5 s.
issues.rule: The threshold is the registry value proto.honkSeconds. The copy must not hard-code a number with no parameter ID.
issues.fix: The car has been blocked too long.
